name: Benson 1996
question: Does abdominal sacral suspension with paravaginal repair yield better outcomes than vaginal sacrospinous suspension with paravaginal repair for significant pelvic support defects?

design.blinding: not reported; postoperative examination by a nonsurgeon coauthor

arms.label: Abdominal colposacral suspension with paravaginal repair
vaginal bilateral sacrospinous vault suspension with paravaginal repair

design.population: Of 101 women assigned, 88 underwent surgery (48 vaginal, 40 abdominal). Eligibility required cervical prolapse to or beyond the hymen, or vaginal vault inversion exceeding half its length with anterior wall descent to or beyond the hymen and a lateral paravaginal defect. Exclusions included more than two prior abdominal pelvic operations, morbid obesity, and prior inflammatory bowel or pelvic disease.
design.description: Prospective randomized abdominal versus vaginal surgical comparison
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1418–1419; Table I

verdictNote: Enrollment stopped early at 88 operations; outcomes were assessed in 80 women.
takeaway: Among 80 evaluated women, abdominal colposacral suspension plus paravaginal repair achieved optimal effectiveness in 22/38 (58%) versus 12/42 (29%) after vaginal bilateral sacrospinous suspension plus paravaginal repair at a mean 2.5 years (reported RR 2.03, 95% CI 1.22–9.83).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Benson JT, Lucente V, McClellan E. "Vaginal versus abdominal reconstructive surgery for the treatment of pelvic support defects: a prospective randomized study with long-term outcome evaluation." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 1996;175(6):1418-1422. doi:10.1016/s0002-9378(96)70084-4
reports.followUp: 1–5.5 years among 80 evaluated women; mean 2.5 years

results.measure: Asymptomatic, apex above levator plate, and no vaginal tissue beyond hymen
results.note: Reported relative risk is for abdominal versus vaginal repair. The paper does not designate a primary endpoint or provide a P value for this comparison; the reported 95% CI is 1.22–9.83.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1419; Results, p 1420

results.measure: Symptomatic, apex descent greater than half its length, or vaginal wall beyond hymen; reported with reoperation
results.note: Reported relative risk is for vaginal versus abdominal repair. The paper does not designate this as a secondary endpoint or provide a P value for this comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1420; Results, p 1420

results.measure: Asymptomatic and improved prolapse without meeting optimal criteria
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, p 1420

delivery.label: Enrollment and early stopping
delivery.value: The calculation targeted 124 women (62 per arm) to detect a 20% difference with 80% power at alpha 0.05. Of 101 assigned, 10 declined surgery and 3 assigned to abdominal surgery requested vaginal surgery and were withdrawn. Eighty-eight underwent surgery and 80 were evaluated. The trial stopped after interim analysis found an outcome disparity.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 1418–1419; Results, p 1420

delivery.label: Procedures and follow-up examination
delivery.value: Both arms used permanent monofilament suture for paravaginal repair. Vaginal surgery used bilateral sacrospinous vault suspension; abdominal surgery used colposacral suspension. Hysterectomy was performed in 24/48 vaginal and 20/40 abdominal cases; autologous sling urethropexy in 10/48 and 2/40, respectively. A nonsurgeon coauthor examined women at 6 months and annually to 5 years, standing at maximum strain.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Table II, pp 1419–1420

delivery.label: Catheter use, operative time, and hospital charge

values.exp: Catheter use >5 days 48% (reported); operating time 215 ± 47 minutes; hospital charge $8,048 ± $2,623
values.ctl: Catheter use >5 days 75% (reported); operating time 196 ± 38 minutes; hospital charge $6,537 ± $851

delivery.locator: Full text, Tables III and V, p 1420
delivery.note: The paper gives percentages but no counts for catheter use beyond five days; these percentages do not reconcile exactly with the table's evaluated-arm denominators. Tables III and V mark catheter use, operating time, and hospital charge P < .05.
